description: ESP32-S3 + 8 MB PSRAM + OV2640 camera + PDM mic + microSD; male headers factory-soldered (pins expected on the side opposite the Sense board — UNVERIFIED)
why: Same board as stage0-devkit.csv, but it plugs into the Expansion Board Base instead of needing its 14 header pins soldered
notes: $14.90 excl. VAT on Seeed's own PDF (2026-09); ~$19.95 US street. Fallback if out of stock: the unsoldered 113991115 + a Pimoroni/Adafruit 3662 hammer header (press-fit, fit in the XIAO's holes UNVERIFIED). Header side UNVERIFIED (docs/research/04 §A1): before ordering confirm on the product photo that the pins come out opposite the Sense board; after seating, the first photo (docs/07 §1.5) must not be of the base PCB

part: Seeed Expansion Board Base for XIAO (103030356; Adafruit 5033)
description: Carrier board: XIAO socket, all pins on 2 female breakout headers, 2x Grove I2C + Grove UART + Grove A0/D0, JST 2.0 LiPo socket + charger (460 mA max), user button on D1, passive buzzer on A3/D3, OLED 0x3C, RTC PCF8563 0x51, microSD (CS D2)
why: Replaces the breadboard, the tactile switch, the piezo and the battery wiring: its button IS PIN_BUTTON (D1/GPIO2) and its buzzer IS PIN_BUZZER (D3/GPIO4); the LiPo plugs in
notes: Leave the microSD slot empty (CS = D2, SPI on D8/D9/D10). Never plug a UART Grove device in (D6/D7 are I2S). Whether its charger reaches the XIAO BAT pads or only 5V/VIN is UNVERIFIED (schematic fetch blocked) — the XIAO's own BAT pads stay unused

description: DRV2605L haptic driver (I2C 0x5A) with an ERM coin motor factory-attached; one Grove plug
why: The haptic cue with zero joints: the Adafruit DRV2605L QT breakout (2305) is plug-in on the bus side but its Motor+/Motor- pads need solder. ERM instead of LRA on the bench; firmware HAPTIC_MOTOR_LRA 0 (env xiao_esp32s3_sense_base)
notes: Into Grove I2C socket #1. The LRA feel (INEED LRA0825BC) returns on the stage-1 board; the Grove module's EN is tied on-module, so PIN_HAPTIC is -1 in this build

description: 3-axis accelerometer with click (tap) engine; I2C 0x18 (0x19 with the SDO jumper); INT + I2 through-holes; 2 QT sockets
why: Double-tap = hands-free ask; the LIS2DW12 of stage 1 has no QT/Qwiic breakout, so the firmware detects LIS2DW12 (0x44) or LIS3DH (0x33) at boot (src/imu_lis3dh.cpp)
notes: Alternative: SparkFun Micro LIS3DH Qwiic SEN-29529 ($5.95, 0x19). SparkFun Qwiic LIS2DH12 is retired; Adafruit has no LIS2DW12 board. KX132 Qwiic ($15.50) would need another driver

part: Grove to STEMMA QT / Qwiic / JST SH cable 100 mm (Adafruit 4528 or SparkFun PRT-15109)
description: Grove plug on one end; 4-pin JST SH (STEMMA QT / Qwiic) on the other
why: Feeds the LIS3DH from the base's Grove I2C socket #2 — no soldering and no breadboard
notes: One is enough: the Grove Haptic Motor has its own Grove cable and the base has two I2C Grove sockets, so nothing is daisy-chained

part: Male-male jumper wires (10-20 pcs) + optional hammer-header strip (Adafruit 3662)
description: 0.1 in male-male jumpers; the hammer header is a press-fit (solderless) male header, cut to single pins
why: INT1: LIS3DH INT hole -> base breakout header D8 (GPIO7) for tap-to-wake; D10 -> amp DIN if the speaker is built. The breakout-side end of the INT wire is a friction-fit pin, a tapped-in hammer-header pin, or an IC hook
notes: The INT jumper is OPTIONAL: with -DMCRING_XIAO_BASE the firmware polls the LIS3DH's latched click source every 25 ms and ignores D8 (it floats without the wire); the ring then wakes from deep sleep on the button only. Tap-to-wake needs the jumper AND env xiao_esp32s3_sense_base_tapwake. Hammer-header fit in 1.0 mm breakout holes UNVERIFIED (designed for the Pi's holes); Adafruit 3255 alligator-to-jumper set ($7.95) is the clip alternative

part: LiPo 1S >= 400 mAh with JST-PH 2.0 plug and PCM (Adafruit 3898 400 mAh or 1578 500 mAh)
description: 3.7 V pouch cell with protection circuit; JST-PH plug mates with the base's JST 2.0 socket
why: Battery-powered bench runs; the base charges it from the XIAO's USB. NOT the 100 mAh ring cell (Adafruit 1570): the base's charger is 460 mA max = 4.6 C for that cell
notes: Check red = + against the base's JST silkscreen first — a Seeed forum thread reports reversed pigtails on early units. Battery % stays 'unknown' (255) on this rig: the A0 divider is not built (the cell's + is only on the JST pigtail)

part: Adafruit MAX98357A I2S class-D amp breakout (3006) — OPTIONAL
description: MAX98357A mono amp, 2.5-5.5 V; speaker SCREW TERMINAL pre-soldered since 2024-06; 7-pin header NOT soldered
why: Hear answers from the ring instead of the phone (AUDIO_OUT, F12). The one stage-0 item without a plug-in path for its signal pins: press-fit hammer-header pins + female jumpers, 5 joints at a makerspace, or defer to stage 1 (SMT on the board). Headphones need none of this
notes: BCLK <- D7, LRC <- D6, VIN <- 3V3, GND via a 'Grove to 4-pin male jumper' cable (Seeed 110990210, ~$2.90/5) from the base's Grove UART socket (check the silkscreen for which pin is D6/D7); DIN <- D10 jumper from the breakout header; SD -> VIN; GAIN open (9 dB, keep volume <= 200). STEMMA Speaker 3885 is NOT an alternative (analog in; the ESP32-S3 has no DAC)

part: 8 ohm speaker with leads — OPTIONAL (with the amp): Adafruit 3923
description: Mini oval speaker, 8 ohm 1 W, ~30 mm leads (100 mm on older stock) ending in a 2-pin Molex PicoBlade plug
why: Load for the amp; snip the PicoBlade plug off and strip ~5 mm of each lead (wire stripper, no solder) into the amp's pre-soldered screw terminal. Louder than the ring's 10 mm driver (~66 dB at 1 m), so keep the volume <= 200
notes: Polarity irrelevant. NOT the PUI AS01008MR-2-R (10 mm, the stage-1 part): it has solder-pad terminals (hardware/electrical/out/mcring_v1_bom.csv LS1) — stage-1 only, where its pads get the pigtail joint of docs/10 §7
